Police said Espinosa and Blunt were in adjacent cells and used a long metal wire to scrape away mortar around the cinder block between their cells and the outer wall in Espinosa's cell. Then they jumped a razor-wire fence onto a New Jersey transit railroad bed to freedom, police said. Authorities found two sets of footprints in the snow heading in opposite directions. At a news conference Monday, Romankow read the note that was found in Espinosa's cell, saying it represented the "arrogance of these two men." "Thank you officer -------- for the tools needed, you're a real pal, Happy Holidays," the note read, with a smiley face drawn next to it. Authorities are investigating the note's claims about the guard, the Associated Press reported. The guard has not turned in a report and disciplinary action has not been taken, Romankow said, according to AP. To delay discovery of the escape, Espinosa and Blunt used dummies made of sheets and pillows in their beds. "I think this is a very serious situation you saw," he said. # Two New Jersey Inmates Stage Elaborate Escape, Remain at Large

(CNN) -- Two inmates at New Jersey's Union County Jail orchestrated a daring, cinematic escape Saturday night and remain fugitives as of Monday, according to Union County Prosecutor Ted Romankow.

Twenty-year-old Jose Espinosa and 32-year-old Otis Blunt—both considered armed and dangerous—were discovered missing from their cells at approximately 5:15 p.m. Saturday. In their wake, the men left dummies fashioned to resemble sleeping bodies, traces of cinder block dust, and a note wishing authorities a mocking "Happy Holidays."

Espinosa, who recently pleaded guilty to aggravated manslaughter, had been scheduled for sentencing on January 25 and faced a minimum 17-year prison term. Blunt was being held on $75,000 bond for weapons and robbery charges. Both men had been confined to the jail's high-security wing, according to Romankow.

## A Meticulously Planned Breakout

Investigators say Espinosa and Blunt, housed in adjacent cells, used a length of metal wire to painstakingly scrape away the mortar surrounding a cinder block separating their cells and the outer wall—working from within Espinosa's cell. Once the block was loosened, they shattered it and concealed the fragments in a footlocker.

Blunt, who stands 5-foot-10 and weighs 210 pounds, then squeezed through the resulting gap—roughly 16 to 18 inches wide—to join Espinosa. The pair subsequently forced their way through a similarly sized opening in the outer wall.

From a rooftop landing, the two men leapt approximately 15 feet outward and 30 feet down, Romankow said, before scaling a razor-wire fence onto a New Jersey Transit rail bed and vanishing into the night. Investigators later discovered two sets of footprints in the snow, leading in opposite directions.

## A Taunting Note and Troubling Allegations

At a Monday news conference, Romankow read aloud the note discovered in Espinosa's cell, calling it emblematic of the pair's brazen arrogance. It read: "Thank you officer [redacted] for the tools needed, you're a real pal, Happy Holidays"—accompanied by a hand-drawn smiley face.

According to the Associated Press, authorities are now investigating the note's implication that a guard may have provided assistance. Romankow confirmed that the guard in question has yet to file an incident report, and no disciplinary action has been taken thus far.

## Echoes of "The Shawshank Redemption"

To buy time before their absence was noticed, Espinosa and Blunt constructed makeshift dummies from sheets and pillows, positioning them beneath their blankets. They also concealed the wall openings behind pinup photos of women in bikinis—a detail strikingly reminiscent of the classic prison escape depicted in *The Shawshank Redemption*.

Romankow, however, downplayed the comparison. "I think this is a very serious situation," he remarked. "I'd prefer not to compare it to any film, though I understand why people might, given the obvious similarities. Except in *The Shawshank Redemption*, they had a better poster on the wall."

## Manhunt Underway

Police noted that Blunt had previously attempted a similar escape in September, employing comparable tactics. A reward of $8,000 has been offered for information leading to the capture of either man.

Romankow confirmed that a statewide manhunt is currently underway, with multiple law enforcement agencies coordinating the search.

*CNN's Brian Vitagliano contributed to this report.*

# Prison Break at New Jersey Facility Draws Comparisons to Famous Film

Authorities in Union County, New Jersey are still searching for two prisoners who pulled off a daring breakout that seemed straight out of Hollywood. As of Monday, Prosecutor Ted Romankow confirmed that the fugitives remained on the loose following their Saturday night disappearance.

Guards realized something was wrong around 5:15 p.m. Saturday when they noticed Jose Espinosa, 20, and Otis Blunt, 32, weren't in their cells. In their place, the men had left makeshift dummies in their beds along with dust from broken cinder blocks and a taunting note that read "Happy Holidays" to whoever found it.

Both inmates are being treated as armed and dangerous. Espinosa had just admitted guilt to manslaughter charges and was awaiting a January 25 sentencing that could have put him behind bars for a minimum of 17 years. Blunt, meanwhile, was locked up on robbery and weapons charges, unable to post his $75,000 bail.

The prosecutor noted that despite being housed in the jail's maximum-security wing, the pair managed to exploit their neighboring cell placement to pull off the escape.

## How They Did It

Using nothing more than a lengthy metal wire, the inmates chipped away mortar surrounding a cinder block that separated Espinosa's cell from the outside wall. After working the block loose, they crushed it into smaller fragments and stashed the debris inside a storage locker.

The larger of the two men, Blunt—who stands 5'10" and weighs 210 pounds—managed to force his way through a gap measuring just 16 to 18 inches to reach Espinosa's cell. From there, both men squeezed through a similarly narrow opening they'd created in the building's exterior wall.

Once outside on a rooftop landing, the escapees made a dramatic leap—covering roughly 15 feet horizontally while dropping about 30 feet down, according to Romankow's account. Their escape route continued as they cleared a razor-wire barrier, landing on nearby railroad tracks used by New Jersey Transit. Investigators later discovered two separate trails of footprints in the snow, each heading in a different direction.

## A Mocking Message

During Monday's press briefing, Romankow read aloud the note discovered in the abandoned cell, describing it as evidence of the inmates' brazen attitude. The message thanked an unnamed correctional officer by name for supplying "the tools needed," calling them "a real pal" and wishing "Happy Holidays"—complete with a hand-drawn smiley face.

The Associated Press reported that officials are now looking into whether the note's implication about staff involvement holds any truth. According to Romankow's statements to AP, the officer named in the note hasn't yet filed any paperwork, and no disciplinary measures have been implemented so far.

## Echoes of a Classic Film

To buy themselves extra time before anyone noticed they were gone, the men had stuffed sheets and pillows into bed-shaped forms resembling sleeping bodies. They'd also covered the wall openings with pinup-style photos of women in bikinis—a tactic strikingly similar to the iconic prison escape depicted in "The Shawshank Redemption."

When asked about the resemblance, Romankow downplayed it, though not without a touch of dry humor. "This is genuinely serious business," he remarked. "I'd rather not draw movie comparisons, even though I understand why people would—it does bear a strong resemblance to some films." He couldn't resist adding one dig, however: "Although in 'Shawshank,' they at least had a nicer poster."

## Prior Attempt and Ongoing Search

Records show this wasn't Blunt's first attempt at freedom—he reportedly tried a comparable escape method back in September, though that attempt failed.

An $8,000 bounty now sits on the men's heads as multiple law enforcement agencies coordinate a statewide manhunt to track them down, Romankow confirmed.

*Additional reporting contributed by CNN's Brian Vitagliano.*

# Two New CNN Developments Reshape Deep Learning Landscape

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) continue to evolve, with two new architectural innovations recently capturing attention in the machine learning community. These advances demonstrate how CNNs remain a cornerstone of computer vision despite the rise of transformer-based models.

## The First Innovation: Efficient Feature Extraction

The first new development focuses on improving computational efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. Researchers have introduced novel convolution operations that reduce the number of parameters while maintaining—or even improving—performance on standard benchmarks. This breakthrough addresses one of the longstanding challenges with CNNs: the trade-off between model complexity and inference speed. By restructuring how convolutional layers process spatial information, these new techniques allow CNNs to run effectively on edge devices with limited computational resources.

## The Second Innovation: Hybrid Architecture Design

The second major advancement involves combining CNNs with attention mechanisms in new hybrid architectures. Rather than viewing CNNs and transformers as competing paradigms, researchers have found ways to leverage the strengths of both approaches. CNNs excel at capturing local spatial patterns through their inherent inductive biases, while attention mechanisms are adept at modeling long-range dependencies. This new fusion approach has shown promising results in tasks ranging from image classification to object detection, often outperforming pure CNN or pure transformer models on specific benchmarks.

## Why These Two Developments Matter

Together, these two new directions illustrate that CNNs are far from obsolete. Instead, they are being reimagined and integrated into more sophisticated systems. The efficiency-focused innovation makes CNNs more accessible for real-world deployment, particularly in mobile and IoT applications where computational resources are constrained. Meanwhile, the hybrid architecture approach pushes the boundaries of what's possible in terms of accuracy and versatility.

## Looking Ahead

As the field continues to advance, these two new CNN developments serve as a reminder that innovation in deep learning isn't always about replacing older techniques—it's often about refining and combining them in creative ways. CNNs, first popularized decades ago, continue to prove their relevance by adapting to new challenges and integrating with emerging technologies. This ongoing evolution ensures that convolutional architectures will remain a vital tool in the deep learning toolkit for years to come.
